### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8bc080847291127d590cb260215a7ce652603d43`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8bc080847291127d590cb260215a7ce652603d43` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `67a7dbd26521767a579382080822f6d6d7c9f50a` — the merge of head `6acd3f1290e7bd689f2bca73b94c252cf49696b6` into base `8bc080847291127d590cb260215a7ce652603d43`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 67a7dbd26521767a579382080822f6d6d7c9f50a && git checkout 67a7dbd26521767a579382080822f6d6d7c9f50a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8bc080847291127d590cb260215a7ce652603d43 6acd3f1290e7bd689f2bca73b94c252cf49696b6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8bc080847291127d590cb260215a7ce652603d43 && git merge --no-ff 6acd3f1290e7bd689f2bca73b94c252cf49696b6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8bc080847291127d590cb260215a7ce652603d43
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8bc080847291127d590cb260215a7ce652603d43` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: REWORK** · PR #34644 · card #34441 (Fixes) · first review · L1-c2 of seat repo:objectstack#2 · read 2026-11-17T06:06Z

Head-sha: `1aff827bd5dde367bc1f7b7280681b403561b6f1` (the head of final-head comment 6940187329)

Read from GitHub and the diff at this head (merge base `31096af83d`), not from the report. 6 files, +235/−29.

**Checked and holding**
- **Shape.** The PR is a draft against `main`. The body opens with `Fixes #34441`, which is right because the acceptance as narrowed by 6938023903 is met in full. No closing keyword sits next to another open card. The changeset is `patch` on both touched published packages and carries the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol` and `Skills-docs:` lines. `skills/**` has no sentence on bundle members naming no package, so `Skills-docs: none` stands. The ADR-0087 marker is present, and `18.shipped-base-dependent-canonical-row-not-published.ts` registers the `/published` narrowing.
- **Cell 1, orphan arm.** `isWantedMember(code)` is added to the #28409 orphan condition. Naming no member, `wantedMember` is the canonical one. A's shipped `fr-FR` is then no code layer of the addressed member, so D's `en-US` row is no longer an orphan, and `/published` stops serving it. A read that names `fr-FR` keeps the old condition.
- **Cell 1, code-layer fallback.** It applies only when `code === null`, `member === undefined` and there is no bare-action answer. It is the same `lookupArtifactItem` without the member argument. For a type with no bundle members, `wantedMember` is undefined, so the earlier lookup was the same call and nothing moves there. The new call site is recorded in `protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts` with disposition `no`.
- **Cell 2, `rowHeldBaseAddressOf` split.** The old exclusions keep their order: no shipper, `readsByPackage`, no environment item, the per-row rules, exactly one base, and a pair among holders. The new arm returns the base only when the base itself has a row at the member and `atMember.size >= 2`. The S1 guard still covers the arm for "a member only additions hold". Every caller is a read path: item face 473 and 810, layered 111 and 240. No write path calls it. Both refusal sites keep the refusal beside a package-less row (`!holding.unbound`, `!address.unbound`, #33210).
- **One read (#24371).** `judgeHost.readItemActiveRows` returns the rows already read for the same `(type, name)`, and `storedRowHoldersRefusal` passes `activeRows` as `preread`. Ablation 6 (lane-reported) is the CI red at `d4500af0`.
- **Gates.** 71 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 58 `success`, 13 `skipped`, 0 failed. Lane readings: metadata-protocol 23046 passed, objectql `src/protocol*` 1189/1189, served-stack 159/159, 93/93 derived gates exit 0, and the `!` battery VERDICT 0 (4055 passed). The ablations are lane-reported, and I did not re-run them.

**R1 (REWORK) · cell 2's moved answers are listed and pinned only at `?member=en-US`, but the new arm moves the canonical member, which a read naming no member also addresses.** The new arm in `rowHeldBaseAddressOf` answers "at ANY member the base itself holds as a row (the canonical one included)". `en-US` is the canonical member, and `member === undefined` resolves to it in `overlayMemberWhere`. So in the cell-2 shape, these doors take the same new arm:
- the plain read naming no member (`GET /meta/email_template/sharedmail`, item face 810 and 473);
- `/layers` naming no member (layered 111 and 240);
- `/published`;
- the execution read naming no member.

On `main` the S1 guard returned `undefined` for the canonical member, so these reach the two-holder refusal just as `?member=en-US` did. The changeset's moved-answer list, the body's FROM→TO table and the S2 pins name only `?member=en-US`, `/layers?member=en-US` and the execution read at `member: 'en-US'`. The doors naming no member are neither listed nor pinned, in either holding or on either side of a reboot. Acceptance item 1 is about exactly these doors ("`/published`, `/layers` and the plain read naming no member give one answer before and after a restart").

Required:
- In the S2 `observe`, add the plain read, `/layers` and `/published` naming no member, and the execution read naming no member. Assert each for the row-held holding and the shipped CONTROL, before and after a reboot, with `status` and `code` on any refusal (ADR-0112).
- List each door that moves in the changeset's cell-2 bullet and the body's FROM→TO table. List each door that does not move under "Not moved".
- If one of them answers differently from the plain read, say which and why in the body.

**Deviation for the seat, not a REWORK item**: premise correction 6938023903 said the fix "does not touch `packages/spec/src`". The ADR-0087 entry for the `/published` narrowing now does. Under rule card #34424, that is a large-card trigger. The work is done, and the landing tier below already accounts for it.

**L2 owed: yes.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and a new `packages/spec/src` entry put it at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` for the whole diff outside the prose face, through this account's review seat, on the head after R1.

**Landing tier**: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34644` reports NOT governed, +235/−29 = 264 lines ≤ 3000. The PR touches `packages/spec/src` and declares a narrowing, so under the seat's 03:21Z and 04:14Z orders it lands **Tier H via the seat**, not as an area landing. It stays draft.

### ① Derived judgments

Cell 1 (base A ships `email_template` N in `fr-FR` only; dependent D, which declares A, stores the canonical `en-US` row). Doors naming no package:

Both align the two sides of a restart.
- Each door now gives one answer across a restart. The doors do not agree with each other (`/published` 404, item read and `/layers` 200 A's `fr-FR`): that is the baseline with no D row, scoped out by 6938023903.

Cell 2 (no shipper; A stores `en-US`, D stores `en-US` and `fr-FR`), bundled type:
- Item read `?member=en-US`, `/layers?member=en-US`, the execution read: 409 naming A and D, now 200 A's row, before and after a restart, pinned. Right for a bundled type: the registry's own count (`isBundleAddition` with `codeMembersOf`, #33127) makes a member both hold only as stored rows no clash, so D is an addition and A the one holder.
- `/published` (it reads the canonical member, and asks the item read first): 409, now 200 A's row, by code read. A moved door the changeset does not list and no test pins (S2).

Call-site ledger: the one new `lookupArtifactItem` site is recorded with disposition `no`; right, the fallback is the code layer and grafts nothing. For a type with no members the fallback repeats the lookup above it with the same arguments and cannot change an answer.

### ② Semver level

Both `Check Changeset` runs and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are green on the head. The level holds; the body's list of moved answers does not (S2).

- Serial constraint with PR #34347 and PR #34238 (the dev's flag): a lane matter; the fallback sits below the line #34347 edits. Not judged here.

- Card acceptance 1 as filed (the three doors agree with each other) and acceptance 3 (a CONTROL with the base shipping `en-US`) were narrowed by 6938023903 to the answers with no D row. The residue is `main`'s baseline and belongs on a follow-up card: `/published` 404 beside an item read of 200 A's `fr-FR`, and `?member=en-US` 404 beside the member-less read's 200 although `resolveBundleMemberSelector` calls them the same request.
- Tier H step for the `packages/spec/src` path: the seat's, after this record.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The row-grain judgment reads one item's active rows by `(type, name)` and needs the manifests' dependency closure, which is not in SQL. The item face still reads them once (the head's judge-host reuse; the objectql one-read pins are green). The layered path gains one such read (N2).
- Access: no finding. Every moved answer serves a row or code layer the same caller already reads at an exact address, or names fewer packages than the refusal it replaces.

### ④ Design judgment

The entry (the `hits` file). It holds. Type `SemanticMigration`, the four required fields present, filename derived from the id, no index owed (the directory is the registry, generated), `relevantWhen` rightly omitted with the reason in the comment, and the same shape as its sibling `18.row-held-base-addition-bare-read-at-base.ts`. It rightly covers the narrowing alone.

The narrowing. It makes the published rule real and takes no declared capability away. `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` and the ADR-0146 paragraph of the platform skill on `main` say a dependent's added locale is that package's own item, served only under its own `?package=`; `/published` serving it at the bare address, and only until a restart, was the implementation gap. D's row stays readable at its own address. The orphan report keeps every case it was written for: with a member named, the code layer is always that member's, and a base shipping the canonical member still reports a dependent's row of it.

M1 (must-fix) — `rowHeldBaseJudgment` runs for types with no bundle members, and moves their refusal. On `main` the first guard of `rowHeldBaseAddressOf` (`overlayMemberValue` must be a string) returned before anything else for the canonical member and for every type with no members. The diff moves that guard into the tail arm, so the new arm (`atMember.has(base)` with two or more packages at the member) is reached for every type `readsByPackage` answers true for: app, page, dashboard, report, tool, permission, flow and the rest of `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`. For such a type `overlayMemberWhere` is empty, so every row of the name is at the member. A name no package ships, held as stored rows by A and by D where D declares A, therefore moves on the item read, the execution read, `/layers` and `/published` from 409 naming A and D (the #32607 refusal) to A's row. Nothing supports it: the docblock still says the arm applies only to a bundled type; the stated ground, that the registry names the base the one holder, is false there (`packageScopedHoldersOf` returns every holder when the type has no discriminator; a bundle addition exists only for a bundled type); the changeset's list of every moved answer does not carry it; and no test pins it (the existing dashboard and tool pins use packages with no dependency between them, which is why the checks are green). It also reaches `getMetaItemLayered` naming no package for `permission`, the read the security catalog echo and the packaged-permission-set lock gate take, against the note at the top of that function that those readers keep the answer they had. Fix: keep the judgment to bundled types (a discriminator guard at the top of `rowHeldBaseJudgment`) and pin a non-bundled name with a dependent and a base both holding rows as still refused on every bare door; or take the move to a ruling and then declare and pin it.

S1 (should-fix) — the contract of `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` is now false and the diff leaves it. The function body says the class method's docblock is its contract; that docblock (`protocol.ts`) says the door refuses whenever the item's active rows at the member are bound to two or more packages, with the refusal the package-less save and delete answer for the same rows, one answer to one ambiguity. In cell 2 the door now serves A's stack while the save, delete, publish and history doors naming no package still refuse the same rows naming A and D, the Studio shape that docblock describes: the view loads, the save it then sends is refused. Fix: state the exception and the remaining refusal of the writes in that docblock and in the changeset, and open a follow-up card for whether the writes naming no package follow the base.

S2 (should-fix) — the changeset's list headed every moved answer is incomplete, and one of the missing moves is unpinned. Missing: cell 2 `/published` (409 to A's row), which no assertion covers; cell 1 `/layers` naming no member before a restart, whose `overlay` moves from D's row to null (pinned, not listed). Fix: add both to the changeset and the PR table, and add `/published` to the `S2` pin for the row-held and the shipped holdings.

N1 (nit) — the entry's `acceptanceCriteria` says callers read the row with `?package=DEPENDENT&member=CANONICAL instead` without naming the door; `/published` takes neither parameter, so name the item read as `replacement` does.
N2 (nit) — `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` and `getMetaItemLayered` each call `rowHeldBaseAddressOf` without rows already read, and since the guard moved, the layered read reads the item's active rows once more for every member-less read of a row-only name. M1's guard removes it for types with no members.
N3 (nit) — the first paragraph of the `rowHeldBaseAddressOf` docblock still says the read moves only when the base holds no row at the member and only at a named non-canonical member, which the appended paragraph reverses; the `storedRowHoldersRefusal` docblock still states the refusal without the exception.
